data.name: Cyborg Rage
data.detailed_description:
Cyborg Rage is a multiplayer coop space shooter that is all about cooperative online action: Work with your brave wingman to destroy all enemy starships or be destroyed! Master the advantages of your ship class to withstand your enemies!

Cyborg Rage is your source for fast-paced action, massive explosions and a cooperative gameplay core for two pilots that demands good reflexes and fast strategic decisions.

Face the future


The year 3226: The future. Battle Cyborgs were never designed to be smart or develop any kind of self-awareness. They had been produced in masses as expendable military units. It was a time when security was more valuable than freedom. We sent them to the frontlines.

Today, they return.

Choose your ship


Combine your ship technologies with those of your wingman for a maximum of cooperation!

Depending on your chosen ship, your arsenal may include a destructive EMP missile, a missile barrage, instant shield rechargers, an electric field, a nano repair impulse, a massive shield, the devouring nuclear missile... and more technologies that will leave your enemies without doubt who is dominating this sector in space.

Pilots unite


Make one of your friends your trusted wingman or let the matchmaking find a player of your skill level to face the challenge together! Just remember: For the moment, you two rely on each other!

FEATURES


• Top Down Arcade Shooter
• Cooperative Online Multiplayer for two pilots
• Matchmaking with adjusting difficulty
• Rank up in 5 Leagues
• Achieve medals
• Unlock artwork in the gallery
• Single Player Campaign
• 3 Button Mouse, Gamepad and Keyboard Controls


Resistance is futile. You will be assimilated. Buy Cyborg Rage today!

reviews.review:
Cyborg Rage is a cooperative arcade space shooter that builds its identity around straightforward combat, complementary spacecraft abilities, and the idea that two pilots are stronger when they work together. Developed by Ragiva Games and published by Black Shell Media, it presents a futuristic conflict in which humanity must face powerful Battle Cyborgs that have grown beyond their original purpose. Rather than investing heavily in elaborate storytelling, the game quickly establishes its science-fiction premise and uses it as a backdrop for energetic battles filled with enemy ships, missiles, defensive systems, and explosions.

The story takes place in a distant future where Battle Cyborgs, originally created as expendable military units, have become a serious threat to humanity. The premise gives the action a suitably dramatic reason to exist, although narrative depth is not the game's primary concern. There are no extensive character arcs or complicated political themes driving the experience. Instead, the setting provides atmosphere while allowing players to concentrate on piloting their ships and destroying increasingly dangerous opposition. This direct approach suits the arcade nature of the game, although anyone expecting a story-driven science-fiction adventure may find the narrative component rather lightweight.

Combat revolves around maneuvering through hostile encounters, firing on enemies, avoiding damage, and making effective use of specialized technologies. The selection of abilities is one of the more appealing parts of the design. EMP missiles, missile barrages, electric fields, shields, repair impulses, shield-recharging systems, and nuclear weapons introduce different offensive and defensive possibilities. Individually these mechanics are easy to understand, but their usefulness becomes more apparent when two players coordinate their equipment. One pilot can focus on aggressive attacks while another provides protection or recovery, creating a basic but satisfying tactical relationship.

Cooperative play is therefore the game's most distinctive feature. Two players can enter battle together, with the mechanics encouraging them to operate as partners rather than two unrelated ships occupying the same battlefield. Bringing a friend along as a wingman makes encounters considerably more entertaining because communication can turn otherwise simple firefights into coordinated assaults. Matchmaking provides another avenue for finding a partner, and the game's difficulty adjustment is intended to help create reasonably appropriate challenges. Successful cooperation becomes particularly rewarding during crowded battles where a timely shield, repair ability, or powerful attack can rescue the team.

A single-player campaign is also available, allowing the experience to remain accessible when another human pilot is unavailable. This is a welcome feature because it prevents the game's core content from being completely dependent on an active multiplayer population. However, playing alone does expose the simplicity of the underlying shooter more clearly. The cooperative concept is responsible for much of the game's personality, and without another person making decisions alongside you, encounters can become repetitive sooner. It remains functional as a solo arcade shooter, but multiplayer is where its mechanics make the strongest impression.

Progression adds some incentive to continue playing beyond individual battles. Players can advance through five leagues, collect medals, and unlock artwork for a gallery. These rewards are not especially complicated, but they give successful runs and continued participation a greater sense of purpose. The system fits the compact arcade structure because it provides recognizable milestones without burying the player beneath extensive inventories, crafting mechanics, or character statistics. Those who enjoy chasing rankings and completion goals may appreciate the additional objectives, even if the progression lacks the depth of a larger action game.

The visual presentation favors bright science-fiction effects over realism. Lasers, missiles, explosions, spacecraft, and various special abilities keep the screen active, while the overall design communicates the fast-moving arcade character effectively. It is not a technically extravagant production, but the presentation is generally appropriate for the scale of the experience. The audio and soundtrack similarly concentrate on supporting the pace rather than becoming major attractions themselves. Together, these elements produce an energetic atmosphere that works best during intense cooperative engagements.

Control options include keyboard, mouse, and gamepad support, although the handling can take some adjustment depending on what players expect from a top-down shooter. Once the control method becomes familiar, the relatively uncomplicated command set allows greater attention to be placed on movement, weapon usage, positioning, and cooperation. Controller support is particularly relevant for players who prefer an arcade-style setup rather than remaining tied exclusively to keyboard and mouse input.

Steam Deck compatibility is less certain. Cyborg Rage does not have a clearly established official Steam Deck Verified or Playable designation, so it should be treated as an unverified title rather than assumed to offer a completely trouble-free handheld experience. Its controller-oriented gameplay and relatively modest graphical demands suggest that the fundamental game concept is suitable for portable play, but compatibility can involve more than performance alone. Interface behavior, text readability, multiplayer functionality, and any platform-specific issues may require additional attention. Steam Deck owners should therefore approach it as an unsupported or unverified experience rather than expecting the guarantees associated with an official compatibility rating.

The largest weakness is repetition. Enemy encounters, shooting, defensive maneuvering, and ability activation form a satisfying foundation, but there is not enough mechanical variety to keep that foundation feeling fresh indefinitely. More distinctive enemies, environments, objectives, and encounter structures could have given the campaign greater longevity. The progression features soften this problem, yet they cannot completely compensate for the relatively narrow gameplay loop. This makes Cyborg Rage better suited to shorter sessions than prolonged play.

Taken as a compact cooperative arcade shooter, Cyborg Rage offers an entertaining combination of accessible combat and teamwork-focused mechanics. Its assortment of ship technologies gives partners opportunities to support each other, while solo play, matchmaking, leagues, medals, and gallery unlocks broaden the package. Limited variety and repetitive encounters keep it from becoming an exceptional shoot 'em up, but its cooperative foundation provides enough personality to make it worth considering for players who enjoy uncomplicated science-fiction action with a friend.

Rating: 7/10
